title: Interest rates and Bank Rate: our latest decision
summary: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee held the Bank Rate at 3.75% on 19 March 2026, marking the sixth consecutive hold following a series of cuts since August 2024. The Committee cited the war in the Middle East as a key disruption to global energy supplies, which will push UK inflation higher than previously expected in the near term. Current inflation stands at 3.3%, well above the 2% target.
key_points: Bank Rate maintained at 3.75% — sixth hold since cutting began in August 2024
War in the Middle East has disrupted energy transportation and supply chains, raising global energy prices
UK inflation expected to be higher than anticipated in the short term due to energy cost pressures
The MPC acknowledged that monetary policy cannot directly affect global energy prices
The Committee will monitor the situation closely and adjust policy as needed to achieve the 2% inflation target sustainably over the medium term
why_it_matters: The BoE's decision to hold rates signals caution amid external energy supply shocks, suggesting the Committee is willing to tolerate elevated inflation temporarily rather than risk over-tightening. Market participants will watch for whether higher-for-longer energy costs delay the path back to target, which could shift rate cut expectations and affect gilt yields, mortgage rates, and pound sterling positioning.
macro_context: The BoE faces a stagflationary headwind: energy-driven inflation pressures coinciding with slower economic growth as higher fuel costs squeeze household disposable income and business input costs. The Committee's explicit acknowledgment that inflation will be higher than expected signals a more uncertain trajectory for the 2% target, potentially delaying further easing and keeping monetary policy restrictive for longer.
